 JUDGMENT

This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.70,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Sheik Sultan Kutbuddin who met with road traffic accident.
2. The petition averments in brief are that: On 20-12-2022 at about 01-00 p.m., the deceased was riding Scooter Reg.No.KA-15-EM-6602 towards Ayappa Temple Junction to Sarajpur main road.

When he reached near Koramangala 100 feet road, Kendriya Sadan, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Water Tanker Reg.No.KA-51-B- 2870 came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased scooter result of which, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately the deceased was shifted to Kaveri Hospital, Bangalore wherein first aid treatment was given and then he was shifted to Manipal Hospital, Bengaluru.
In spite of better treatment, the deceased succumbed to the injuries on 20-01-2023.
So far, the petitioners have spent Rs.30,00,000/- towards treatment, transportation and funeral and obsequies ceremonies expenses.
3. Prior to the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy.

The deceased was aged about 78 years,
working as a business man and getting income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden demise of deceased, the petitioners have sustained mental and physical hardship.
Hence, 1st respondent is the owner and 2nd respondent is the insurer of the offending vehicle is jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
4. In spite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 remained absent, hence he was placed ex-parte.

5. Respondent No.2- the insurer of Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B-2870 has filed the written statement and admitted the coverage of insurance policy and the liability if any subject to Shamshad Begum vs Govindappa on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87617852/
2 the terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It is contended that the driver of insured vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving license as on the date of accident.

It is further contended that the investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the said driver u/Sec.3 (1),
181, 5(1) 180 for not having valid and effective driving license.
They have denied that the petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they are the dependents on the income of the deceased.
It is further contended that the insured vehicle is not involved in the alleged accident and caused any accident to the deceased as stated in the petition or in the crime records.

6. It is further contended that as on the date of accident the deceased himself was negligent who rode his scooter in a zig zag manner without having proper look over the oncoming vehicles in the road, suddenly took turn without taking precautionary measures , lost control over the vehicle and fell down on the road due to skid and fall but the petitioners in collision with the jurisdictional police have created false crime records and false story about the manner and involvement of the insured vehicle to get the compensation.
7.

On the basis of the rival pleadings following issues have been framed;
1.

Whether the petitioners prove that , Sheik Sultan Kutbuddin was died on account of road traffic accident on 20-12- 2020 at about 01-00 p.m., near Koramangala 100 feet road, near Kendriya Sadan, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B- 2870?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?

3 . What Order or Award?
8.
In order to prove the case, 2nd petitioner got examined himself as PW.1 and one witness is examined as PW.2 and got marked in all 12 documents as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.12 and closed their side.
On the other hand, the driver of the offending vehicle by name Nagaraja K R is examined as RW.1 and got marked document as per Ex.R1 and R2.

The respondent no.2 examined its Senior Manager as RW.2 and got marked copy of policy and terms and conditions as per Ex.R3.
9.
Heard arguments of learned counsel for petitioners and respondent no.2 and perused the entire materials placed on record.

10. My findings on the above issues are as follows:
Issue No.1: In the Affirmative Issue no 2: Partly in the Affirmative Issue No.3: As per final order, for the following;

sentences.text: Issue No.1 :- Petitioners have categorically contended that on the date of accident, the deceased was riding a Scooter Reg.No.KA-15-EM-6602 towards Ayappa Temple Junction to Sarajpur main road.

When he reached near Koramangala 100 feet road, Kendriya Sadan, Bengaluru, at that time the driver of Water Tanker Reg.No.KA-51-B-2870 (hereinafter referred to as the offending vehicle)
came at high speed in a rash and negligent manner dashed against the deceased scooter result of which, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on 20- 01-2023.
12. In order to substantiate the petition averments, the petitioner No.2 got examined himself as PW1.
In the examination in chief, the Pw1 has reiterated the petition averments.

In support of the contention, he has produced 5 documents which are at Ex.P1 to Ex.P5 i.e., F.I.R., along with complaint, spot mahazar, sketch, PM report and Charge sheet are the material documents to prove the present issue.
13.

On the basis of the complaint lodged by Sri Kashif Ahmed who is the brother of deceased, case has been registered against the driver of offending vehicle in Crime No 0063/2022 of Madivala Traffic Police Station for the offence punishable under section 279, 304(A) of IPC.

The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC and u/Sec.3(1), 181, 5(1), 180 of MV Act.

14. As per the case of petitioners , at the time of accident the deceased was proceeding towards Sarajpur main road and at the spot of accident when deceased was standing in his vehicle to take right turn , at that time the offending vehicle which came from Sarajpur main road towards Iyappa Temple in a rash and negligent manner hit against the motorcycle of the deceased.

The PW.1 who is the son of the deceased during his cross examination has admitted the suggestion that the accident in question has occurred in the middle of the road and further deposed that his father was standing in the motorcycle near the divider.
If the spot mahazar and sketch is perused, the accident in question has occurred near the divider.
It is a double road and the width of the road is 35 feet each and there is center median in the middle of the road.
As per the spot mahazar there are traces of break mark of the water tanker.
If the sketch is perused, the offending vehicle which came at high speed dashed against the motorcycle of the deceased who was standing near the divider so as to take right turn towards Sarajpur.
Hence, the spot mahazar clearly reveals that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, only the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Admittedly neither the owner nor the driver has challenged the charge sheet.

Further they have not contested the petition either by filing written statement or adducing their evidence and thereby they have not stated the manner in which according to them the accident in question has occurred.
Hence, issue no.1 is answered in the affirmative.

15. Issue No.2:- After considering the materials placed on record and the submission made by the learned counsel for petitioners, it can be said that the deceased was died in the road traffic accident.
It is stated that at the time of accident the deceased was aged about 78 years.
In this regard, the petitioners have produced Aadhaar card of the deceased which reflects the year of birth of deceased as 1944.

As the accident in question has taken place in the year 2022, it can be said that the Shamshad Begum vs Govindappa on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87617852/
4 deceased was aged about 78 years as on the date of accident.
16.

sentences.text:
So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was doing business and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2022, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- per month.

Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
17.
This petition is being filed by the wife and children of the deceased.
From the evidence of PW.1 it can be gathered that the Pw1 is working in CISCO System Company and getting 14 lacks per annum.
The 3rd petitioner is now employed and residing in USA.
Petitioner no.4 being married daughter is residing with her husband in the matrimonial house.

Hence, though petitioner no.2 to 4 are the legal representatives of the deceased but they are not the dependents of the deceased and petitioner no.1 being the wife of the deceased alone is the dependent of the deceased.

18. Keeping in mind the observation made in Sarala Verma's case reported in 2009 ACJ 1298,
considering the family status of the deceased as deceased had wife and she alone is the dependent of the deceased, hence 1/2 of the annual income is to be deducted towards he personal expenses and remaining 1/2 is to be considered for assessing the compensation under the head loss of dependency.
19. Regarding loss of future prospects, in a ruling reported in 2018 (2) CCC 233 (SC) Munuswamy and Ors / Managing Director Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)

entities.text: Tamil Nadu State Transport Corporation (Villupuram Ltd)
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: where in it was held that while computation of compensation, future prospect of deceased is to be considered by addition to be made to actual income of the deceased which existed at the time of his death.

It is further observed that in case the deceased was self employed or on a fixed salary an addition of 40%
of the established income should be warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years, an addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
Hence in the instant case as the deceased was 78 years no future prospects should be considered.
20. Now by assessing the income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/-, out of it if 1/2 is deducted towards the personal expenses of the deceased it comes around Rs.7,750/-.
The appropriate multiplier applicable for the age group above 65 years is '5'.

Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.4,65,000/- (Rs.7,750/- x 5 x 12 =4,65,000/-).
21.
Because of the untimely death of deceased, petitioner no.1 has lost her husband, petitioner no.2 to 4 lost their father.

So far as quantum of compensation awarded under the head loss of consortium, towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses is concerned slab has been fixed in Pranay Sethi's case reported in AIR 2017 SC 5157.

In para 61 of the said judgment the reasonable figures on conventional heads namely loss of estate, loss of consortium, and funeral Shamshad Begum vs Govindappa on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87617852/
5 expenses should be Rs.15,000/, Rs.40,000/- and Rs.15,000/- respectively.
It is further observed that the aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The judgment in Pranay Sethi's case was rendered on 30th October 2017.

22. As per the observation made in Janabai W D/o Dinkarrao Ghorpade & Ors., Vs. M/s I.C.I.C.I Lambord Insurance Co.Ltd., The Hon'ble Supreme court awarded spousal consortium for wife,
parental consortium and filial consortium.

sentences.text: This was the terms of the judgment in National Insurance Company Ltd / Pranay Sethi and Ors.

By applying the observation made in the aforesaid case, as more than 6 years has lapsed from the date of order amount of consortium fixed in Pranay Sethi's Case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Hence, this court deems it appropriate to award compensation of Rs.48,400/- each to the petitioners under the head loss of consortium.
Accordingly, the funeral expenses and loss of estate should be enhanced from Rs.15,000/- to Rs.18,150/-,
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and Rs 18,150/- towards loss of estate.
23. The petitioners have stated that the deceased was taken treatment at Kavari Hospital and Manipal Hospital and they have spent huge amount towards medical expenses.
In this regard the petitioner have produced discharge summary of Kaveri Hospital and inpatient final bill of Kaveri Hospital and Manipal Hospital and medical bills and prescriptions at Ex.P7.

If Inpatient final bill of Manipal Hospital at Ex.P9 is perused, the inpatient final bill is amounting to Rs.20,31,366/- out of which Rs.14,00,000/- was covered under United Health Care Private Limited and sum of Rs.6,31,366/- is paid by the patient party.
In the Ex.P9 there are payment details of the payment of sum of Rs.6, 31,366/- made by the patient party.
Hence, sum of Rs.6,31,366/- paid by the petitioners is to be considered to assess the compensation under the head medical expenses.
Further if the detailed inpatient bill issued from Kavari Hospital is perused, the total bill amount paid by the petitioners is Rs.22,000/-.

The petitioner in further has produced medical bill for Rs.6,727/-,
Rs.953/-, Rs.377/- and Rs.2,137/- hence, total medical expenses incurred by the petitioners comes around Rs.6,63,560/-.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for compensation under the head medical expenses to the tune of Rs.6,63,560/-.
24.

In the circumstances, the loss assessed by the petitioners due to the death of deceased is calculated as follows:
1 Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
 2 Transportation and funeral  expenses Rs. 18,150/-
 3 Loss of spousal consortium, Rs.1,93,600/-
 parental consortium and filial  consortium (Rs.48,400x4)
 4 Loss of Dependency Rs.4,65,000/-

Medical expenses Rs.6,63,560/-

Thus, in all petitioners are entitled to Rs.13,58,460/-

25. As regarding liability is concerned, it is not in dispute that the insurance policy pertaining to the offending vehicle was in force as on the date of accident.
26. The learned counsel for respondent no.2 has seriously disputed the validity of the driving licence held by the driver of the offending vehicle to drive the offending vehicle.

It is submitted that the offending vehicle /water Tanker is a heavy goods vehicle the Gross Vehicle Weight of which is 12,990 kgs, therefore same is not a light motor vehicle , hence it does not come under the definition of Sec.2(21) of the Motor Vehicles Act.
27.

In order to prove that the driver of the offending vehicle was not possessing valid driving licence,
the respondent no.2 has examined witness by name Nagaraj stated to be the RC owner of the offending vehicle as RW.1.

The RW.1 in the evidence in chief itself, at the outset has denied his being the RC owner of the offending vehicle and he pleaded ignorance of the offending vehicle met with an accident and the death of one person due to the said accident.
It is further deposed by RW.1 that he has no vehicle in his name, he do not have driving licence and no notice was issued to him from Madivala Police Station regarding the accident case.

28. The learned counsel for petitioners by cross examining the Rw.1 has brought to the notice of the court that Rw.1 is not the RC owner of the offending vehicle and summons was served to wrong person instead of the RC owner of the offending vehicle by confusing with the identical name Nagaraj.
29.
If the charge sheet and other documents are perused, the date of birth of the RC owner of the offending vehicle is 15-071999.
That means he is aged nearly about 34 years and his name is Nagaraj K R s/o Rajegowda residing at Door No.17/4, Kadavinakote, Holenarasipur, Hassan.
30. But if the Ex.R1 and R2 I.e,. Aadhar card and PAN card of RW.1 is perused, the date of birth of RW.1 is 01-01-1957 that means he is aged nearly about 67 years.
Further the name of the RW.1 is K R Nagaraj but not Nagaraj K R.
Hence, it can be said that RW.1 is not the owner of the offending vehicle.
31. The respondent no.2 in further has examined the official of insurance company as Rw2.

The RW.2 in his evidence has admitted that as per the driving licence of the driver of offending vehicle his date of birth is 15- 071999 and that the driver had valid driving licence to drive light motor vehicles from 2011-2031 and he had driving licence to drive transport vehicle till 17-05-2022.
Admittedly the accident in question has occurred on 20- 12-2022.

Hence, as on the date of accident,
the driver of the offending vehicle had no driving licence to drive transport vehicle and he had Shamshad Begum vs Govindappa on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87617852/
7 driving licence to drive only light motor vehicles.

sentences.text: Per contra, it is vehemently submitted by the learned counsel for petitioners that the Water Tanker which is in question is a light motor vehicle as its un laden weight is 5550 kgs hence the Water Tanker in question is a light motor vehicle as per definition under Sec. 2 (21 ) of Motor Vehicles Act.
Hence, submitted that the driver who was driving Water Tanker was holding driving licence to drive light motor vehicle, hence respondent no.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.

33. The learned counsel for the petitioners at this juncture has referred the judgment rendered by Hon'ble High Court reported in 2017 (2) MACR 1296 (SC) Mukund Dewangan / Oriental Insurance Company Limited.

In the said case observation was made to the effect that "A transport vehicle and omnibus the gross vehicle weight of either of which does not exceed 7500/- would be a light motor vehicle and also motor car or tractor or a road roller, un 7500/- k.g and holder of driving license to drive class of "light motor vehicle" as provide in section 10(2)(d) is competent to drive a transport vehicle or omnibus the gross vehicle weight of which does not exceed 7,500 k.g or a motor car or tractor or road roller, the un laden weight of which does not exceed 7,500 k.g.
That is to say no separate endorsement on the license is required to drive a transport vehicle of light motor cycle class as enumerated above.
A license issued under section 10(2) continues to be valid after Amendment Act 54/1994 and 28/3/2001 in the form.

34. If the documents placed on record more particularly the insurance policy and RC pertaining to the offending vehicle is perused, the un- laden weight of the offending vehicle is 5550 kgs and GVW is 12990 kgs.

35. If Section 2 (21) MV Act is perused; it defines "Light Motor Vehicle" as follows:
"Light Motor Vehicle" means a transport vehicle or omnibus the gross vehicle weight of either of which or a motor car or tractor or road-roller the unladen weight of any of which, does not exceed 1[7500] kilograms"
Section 2(23) of the MV Act defines "Medium Goods Vehicle" as follows:
"Medium Goods Vehicle" means any goods carriage other than a light motor vehicle or a heavy goods vehicle;"
Section 2(16) of the MV Act defines "Heavy Goods Vehicle" as follows:
"Heavy Goods Vehicle" means any goods carriage the gross vehicle weight of which,or a tractor or a road-roller the unladen weight of either of which, exceeds 12,000 kilograms;"
36.
It is not in dispute that the water tanker is a transport vehicle, which means a goods carriage vehicle.

Therefore if transport vehicle is to be considered as light motor vehicle, then the gross Shamshad Begum vs Govindappa on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87617852/
8

sentences.text: vehicle weight shall not exceed 7500 kgs.

In the definition under Section 2(21) of the MV Act, if the vehicle is a transport vehicle or omnibus and it is said that it can be a light motor vehicle, if its "gross vehicle weight" not exceeds 7500 kg, but not the un-laden weight.

The category of un-laden weight is applicable to a motor car or tractor or road roller, then its un-laden weight shall not exceed 7500kg,
then only these three types of vehicles are to be considered as light motor vehicles.

But so far as transport vehicle or omnibus is concerned, if it is said to be a light motor vehicle, then the category is to be determined as to what is the "gross vehicle weight" and if the "gross vehicle weight" does not exceed 7500kg, then it can be considered as light motor vehicle.
The transport vehicle or omnibus shall be considered as light motor vehicle only when gross vehicle weight is less than 7500kg.
Therefore, admittedly, in the present case, water tanker is a transport vehicle.
Therefore, in the present case, whether the water tanker is a light motor vehicle or medium goods vehicle or heavy goods vehicle the criteria is to be considered based on the "gross vehicle weight".
The gross vehicle weight and registered laden weight are one and the same.
In Ex.R3 the gross vehicle weight is mentioned as 12990kg.
The un-laden weight is mentioned as 5550kg, but the un- laden weight is not a deciding factor to classify the vehicle in case of transport vehicle or omnibus.
In the case of transport vehicle or omnibus, the criteria are "gross vehicle weight" or "gross laden weight".
As per the insurance policy and RC , the registered laden weight, which means the gross vehicle weight is 12990kg.
Therefore, as per Section 2(21) of the MV Act, if the gross vehicle weight of the water tanker exceeds 7500 kg, then the water tanker cannot be termed as light motor vehicle.
37. Then coming to the definition of "Medium Goods Vehicle" and "Heavy Goods Vehicle", as per Section 2(23) and Section 2(16) of the MV Act respectively.
"Medium Goods Vehicle" is any goods carriage other than a Light Motor Vehicle or a Heavy Goods Vehicle.
To say a vehicle is heavy goods vehicle the gross vehicle weight exceeds 12000 kg, then it is a Heavy Goods Vehicle.
In the present case, the registered laden weight that means the permitted gross vehicle weight is 12990kg.
Therefore, it is coming in the category of heavy goods vehicle.
Therefore, water tanker is proved to be a heavy goods vehicle as per Section 2(16) of the Act.
38. Hence, the documents placed on record prove that the accused/driver of the offending vehicle was not holding driving licence to drive the water tanker which is a heavy goods vehicle.

39. The learned counsel for petitioners has vehemently submitted that in the event if this court comes to the conclusion that the driver of the offending vehicle had no valid driving licence, then court may order for pay and recovery by directing the Insurance Company at the first instance to pay the compensation and then to recover the same from the owner of the said vehicle.

The learned counsel for the petitioners at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in (2018) 9 SCC 650 between Shamanna & Anr., Vs. Divisional Manager, Oriental Insurance Co.Ltd., & Ors., In (2004) 3 SCC 297 between National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Swaran Singh & Ors., and ILR 2020 KAR 2239 between New India Assurance Co.Ltd., Bijapur by its Divisional Manager Vs. Yallavva & Anr.
40.

sentences.text: It is true that in the aforesaid cases the Hon'ble High Court and Supreme Court has ordered for pay and recover even if the driver of the offending vehicle had no driving license.

But in the present case the observation made in the aforesaid rulings cannot be applied for the reason that the accident in question has occurred on 20-12-2022 and insurance policy as per Ex.R3 was issued on Shamshad Begum vs Govindappa on 7 October, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/87617852/
9 18-08-2022 i.e., subsequent to the amendment to the MV Act.
41.

Now, so for as the liability of insurance company to pay the compensation is concerned the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has vehemently submitted that after amendment to MV Act dated 01.04.2022 no liability can be fixed on insurance company to pay compensation for violation of policy condition including not holding valid driving licence and no order for pay and recovery can be passed.
The learned counsel for respondent no 2 at this juncture has referred the provision of MV Act prior to amendment and post Amendment to Section 149 and 150 of IMV Act.
42. Admittedly the accident in question has occurred on 20-12-2022 i.e subsequent to the amendment dated 1/4/2022.

Hence in view of the amendment to section 149 and 150 of MV Act dated 1/4/2022 no liability can be imposed on the respondent no 2 to pay the compensation and to recover the said compensation from the respondent no1 under pay and recovery theory and liability is to be imposed to pay compensation solely on the respondent no1 who is the owner as he has violated the policy condition by permitting the offending vehicle to drive by accused who had no valid driving license to drive.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
43. Issue No.4: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 to 3 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.13,58,460/- + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on II.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.13,58,960/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakh Fifty Eight Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty only).
A Sum of Rs.13,58,460/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.12,13,760/- Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each.

Out of the amount, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner No.1 on proper identification.
Entire compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioners No.2 to 4 shall be released to petitioners through E-payment on proper identification.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This petition is filed by the petitioners U/s 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 claiming compensation of Rs.70,00,000/- with respect to the death of deceased Sheik Sultan Kutbuddin who met with road traffic accident.
The deceased was aged about 78 years,
working as a business man and getting income of Rs.25,000/- per month.
Due to the sudden demise of deceased, the petitioners have sustained mental and physical hardship.
opennyai_summary.issue:
6. It is further contended that as on the date of accident the deceased himself was negligent who rode his scooter in a zig zag manner without having proper look over the oncoming vehicles in the road, suddenly took turn without taking precautionary measures , lost control over the vehicle and fell down on the road due to skid and fall but the petitioners in collision with the jurisdictional police have created false crime records and false story about the manner and involvement of the insured vehicle to get the compensation.
7.
On the basis of the rival pleadings following issues have been framed;
1.
Whether the petitioners prove that , Sheik Sultan Kutbuddin was died on account of road traffic accident on 20-12- 2020 at about 01-00 p.m., near Koramangala 100 feet road, near Kendriya Sadan, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of Water Tanker bearing Reg.No.KA-51-B- 2870?
2. Whether the petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom?
3 . What Order or Award?
8.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The investigation officer after investigation filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304(A) of IPC and u/Sec.3(1), 181, 5(1), 180 of MV Act.
Hence, the spot mahazar clearly reveals that the rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is the sole cause for the accident.
Hence, only the charge sheet is filed against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Admittedly neither the owner nor the driver has challenged the charge sheet.
Further they have not contested the petition either by filing written statement or adducing their evidence and thereby they have not stated the manner in which according to them the accident in question has occurred.
So far as the avocation and income of the deceased is concerned, as per the case of petitioners,
deceased was doing business and thereby earning Rs.25,000/- p.m.
The petitioners have not produced any documents to prove the income of the deceased.
Hence it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the deceased.
Since accident has occurred in the year 2022, the court has to consider the notional income of the deceased at Rs.15,500/- per month.
Hence taking into consideration the age and year of accident, this court inclines to take the notional income of the deceased as Rs.15,500/- p.m.
17.
Petitioner no.4 being married daughter is residing with her husband in the matrimonial house.
The category of un-laden weight is applicable to a motor car or tractor or road roller, then its un-laden weight shall not exceed 7500kg,
then only these three types of vehicles are to be considered as light motor vehicles.
The transport vehicle or omnibus shall be considered as light motor vehicle only when gross vehicle weight is less than 7500kg.
Therefore, admittedly, in the present case, water tanker is a transport vehicle.
To say a vehicle is heavy goods vehicle the gross vehicle weight exceeds 12000 kg, then it is a Heavy Goods Vehicle.
In the present case, the registered laden weight that means the permitted gross vehicle weight is 12990kg.
Therefore, it is coming in the category of heavy goods vehicle.
Therefore, water tanker is proved to be a heavy goods vehicle as per Section 2(16) of the Act.
38. Hence, the documents placed on record prove that the accused/driver of the offending vehicle was not holding driving licence to drive the water tanker which is a heavy goods vehicle.
opennyai_summary.decision:
Accordingly the petitioners are entitled towards loss of dependency at Rs.4,65,000/- (Rs.7,750/- x 5 x 12 =4,65,000/-).
21.
Accordingly, the funeral expenses and loss of estate should be enhanced from Rs.15,000/- to Rs.18,150/-,
Petitioners are further entitled for funeral expenses to the tune of Rs.18,150/- and Rs 18,150/- towards loss of estate.
Hence in view of the amendment to section 149 and 150 of MV Act dated 1/4/2022 no liability can be imposed on the respondent no 2 to pay the compensation and to recover the said compensation from the respondent no1 under pay and recovery theory and liability is to be imposed to pay compensation solely on the respondent no1 who is the owner as he has violated the policy condition by permitting the offending vehicle to drive by accused who had no valid driving license to drive.
The compensation shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
In the result Issue No.3 is answered partly in the Affirmative.
43. Issue No.4: In the light of findings given on Issue No.1 to 3 , my finding on this issue is as per the following final order.
ORDER The claim petition filed by the petitioners is hereby allowed in part with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.13,58,460/- + cost of Rs.500/- imposed vide order on II.
In all the petitioners are entitled for sum of Rs.13,58,960/- (Rupees Thirteen Lakh Fifty Eight Thousand Nine Hundred Sixty only).
A Sum of Rs.13,58,460/- shall also carry interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of deposit.
The Respondent No.1 is liable to pay compensation and is directed to deposit the compensation along with interest within two months from the date of award.
Out of the compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.12,13,760/- Petitioner No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.48,400/- each.
Out of the amount, 40% of compensation payable to the petitioner No.1 shall be deposited in her name in any nationalized bank of her choice for a period of 3 years and the remaining 60% shall be released to the petitioner No.1 on proper identification.
Entire compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioners No.2 to 4 shall be released to petitioners through E-payment on proper identification.
Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/-.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
It is submitted that the offending vehicle /water Tanker is a heavy goods vehicle the Gross Vehicle Weight of which is 12,990 kgs, therefore same is not a light motor vehicle , hence it does not come under the definition of Sec.2(21) of the Motor Vehicles Act.
27.
Hence, submitted that the driver who was driving Water Tanker was holding driving licence to drive light motor vehicle, hence respondent no.2 is liable to pay compensation to the petitioners.
The learned counsel for the petitioners at this juncture has referred the judgment reported in (2018) 9 SCC 650 between Shamanna & Anr., Vs.
